newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam's leaders set to step down.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam's leaders set to step down.

text.p: Vietnam's septuagenarian president and prime minister were not on a nationwide list of candidates published on Monday for next month's National Assembly election, making it certain they will step down later this year.

President Le Duc Anh and Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet were also absent from a line-up of candidates selected from elite central organisations, on which they would normally have figured if they were to stay on.

Under the constitution, the prime minister and president would have to stand for election to the legislature in order to have their five-year mandates renewed when the new National Assembly convenes in September.
Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi, 80, was also absent from both the province-by-province list which was published in the official daily Nhan Dan and the central organisation line-up.
The party chief is not constitutionally bound to be a member of the National Assembly. However, Muoi's exclusion from the list indicates that his term is unlikely to continue for long.
Although the names of several likely successors from the 18-strong Politburo have been mooted, there are no indications yet that a decision has been made on who will replace the troika.
All three leaders had been expected to stand down at a party congress a year ago, but last-minute manoeuvring meant that they were kept on.

However, 76-year-old Anh suffered a stroke a few months later, and although he has recovered sufficiently to make some brief public appearances, political sources say the army general is not well enough to stay on.
Kiet, 74, whose reform instincts have long been a foil to Anh's conservatism, has indicated on several occasions that he is tired and ready to stand aside for younger blood.
